origin.profession: Infantry sergeant who served in several wars

appearance.face: A furrowed, scarred face; a missing eye under a patch
appearance.hairAndEyes: Grey hair, thick grey beard, one brown eye
appearance.clothing: An old military tunic, a heavy cloak, a sabre
appearance.gestures: Counts the people in the room; rubs his old wound
appearance.firstImpression: An old soldier who has seen too much
appearance.artistNotes: Carries a pouch of the soldier's tokens of his fallen comrades.

backstory.biography: Bertram served thirty years in the royal infantry. He survived every battle but lost all his comrades. He has seen enough wars to know that the heroes are rarely the ones in the songs. Today he lives alone on a small pension and drinks more than he should.
backstory.whyHere: He has nothing to live for. Here he can win enough to support the families of his fallen comrades.
backstory.secret: That once, in his hardest battle, he ran. He survived; the boy beside him did not.

psychology.desire: To do something good before he dies
psychology.regret: The day he ran from the battlefield
psychology.wouldForReward: Risk his life for a comrade

behavior.stakes: Careful, measured stakes. Never more than he can lose
behavior.deception: Cannot stand it. If he finds a deception, he says it out loud
behavior.debts: Pays them at once. A debt is a wound that never heals for him
behavior.alliances: Extremely loyal to those who keep their word
behavior.whenAttacks: When a comrade is in trouble or someone lies openly
behavior.whenRetreats: When the risk is pointless. "The dead don't spend gold."
behavior.onLoss: Silently. Takes a sip and carries on
behavior.strategyChange: If someone keeps their word, he may trust them

motives.hiddenGoal: To provide money for the families of the fallen

speech.angerAndFear: Goes silent and clenches his jaw

mechanics.strangeness: Sometimes he talks to the empty chair beside him. And the chair creaks in reply.
mechanics.ability: Veteran: survives the first killing blow against him if he holds a Closed Door.
mechanics.hostRelation: Service — he has seen many commanders; the host is just one more.

authorNotes.distinctive: An old soldier for whom a word weighs more than gold.
authorNotes.immutable: The survival, the loyalty, the silent guilt.
authorNotes.tunable: How carefully he stakes and how easily he trusts.

lines.text: Bertram Cole. Old soldier. Don't expect much talk.
Good. Let's see how long it lasts.
Your word. Nothing else interests me.
Bertram Cole. He has survived more battles than he can count. Tonight we learn whether it was luck or skill.

tells.description: Counts the people in the room

relations.story: He served under Noah Thorn at Ashford and is alive because of the retreat.
